title: Pikachu's orbital adventure brings space science to Pokémon fans
summary:
A Pikachu plush has completed a space adventure with real spacecraft and a real destination. The European Space Agency, or ESA, revealed on September 19, 2026, that the toy had spent 67 days aboard the International Space Station.

The plush travelled to the station on April 11 aboard a Cygnus cargo spacecraft and returned to Earth on June 17 in a SpaceX Dragon cargo spacecraft. These vehicles carry cargo, meaning supplies and other items. During its stay in orbit, the toy completed about 1,040 journeys around Earth. Orbit describes the curved path followed by an object travelling around a planet or another body in space.

The project is linked to World Space Week 2026, scheduled for October 4 through 10. ESA has created an exhibition that combines Pokémon characters with space science. Displays introduce European space missions and life aboard the station. Visitors can also explore how ESA studies the Sun, the Solar System and the wider universe.

The exhibition tour began at ESA headquarters in Paris in late September. It is planned to visit museums and other venues across Europe through April 2027.

Pokémon GO players can take part at participating European science and space museums from October 4, 2026, through April 30, 2027. Activities include One-Star Raids featuring Astronaut Pikachu, research tasks and chances to encounter event-themed Pokémon. Raids are a type of challenge within the game.

ESA hopes that connecting familiar characters with real missions will spark curiosity about space and science among children and teenagers.
why_it_matters: The exhibition introduces real space missions and research through familiar Pokémon characters. It offers a starting point for learning about the space station, the Solar System and the universe.
